title: Introduction to cancer biology and lecture learning outcomes
why: The lecturer introduces the cancer biology lecture series, course learning outcomes, and interdisciplinary context for the students.

title: Accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
why: The lecturer explains the conceptual model of stepwise genetic, epigenetic, and viral changes that drive malignant transformation.

title: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
why: The lecturer describes normal differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization, framing cancer as a failure of these developmental programs.

title: Tumour cell culture and the limitations of studying isolated cells
why: The lecturer moves from histological examination of tissue invasion to experimental methods for culturing cancer cells in dishes and the need for 3D culture models.

title: Invasion as the distinction between benign and malignant tumours
why: The lecturer contrasts benign and malignant tumors based on invasion through basement membranes and routes of metastatic spread.

title: Routes of metastasis and features of secondary tumours
why: explains how cancer cells spread to distant sites through various anatomical routes and presents examples of secondary metastases

title: Histological comparison of benign tumours and invasive malignancy
why: The lecturer contrasts encapsulated benign lesions with invasive malignant tumors to illustrate how local tissue invasion appears histologically and anatomically.

title: Colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma progression and histological assessment of invasion
why: The lecturer examines colorectal histology to demonstrate how benign adenomatous polyps transition into invasive adenocarcinomas.

title: Malignant potential and harmful effects of benign tumours
why: The lecturer discusses why benign tumors vary in progression to malignancy and how they can still cause severe clinical harm.

title: Tumour nomenclature by tissue of origin and malignant status
why: The lecturer explains the naming rules and common exceptions for benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

title: Mechanisms of cancer-related illness and death
why: The lecturer details the direct physical, systemic, and metastatic mechanisms through which cancer causes illness and death.

title: Incidence and mortality of major human tumour types
why: The lecturer compares tumor incidence across human tissue types, companion animals, and diverse multicellular organisms.

title: Tumour incidence across animal species
why: The lecturer examines tumor prevalence across other animal species to show that cancer is a fundamental disorder of differentiation in multicellular organisms.

title: Clinical presentation of cancer and the rationale for screening
why: The lecturer outlines typical clinical presentations and evaluates population screening approaches for cervical, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancers.

title: Cervical screening for HPV-associated pre-invasive lesions
why: The lecturer explores cervical cancer screening in depth, explaining the anatomy, squamo-columnar histology, HPV progression to dysplasia, and Pap smear cytology.

title: Methods and limitations of colorectal, breast and prostate cancer screening
why: The lecturer shifts to colorectal cancer screening along with comparisons to breast and prostate screening programs.

title: Lecture close: learning outcomes, revision and upcoming practicals
why: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap reference to learning outcomes and notices for upcoming practicals and lectures.
